extracted.intended_audience: debt collectors, compliance officers, and legal counsel responsible for FDCPA/Regulation F compliance
extracted.subtask_short: FDCPA Reg F compliance for debt collectors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and commentary interpreting 12 CFR part 1006 (Regulation F) explaining required practices and prohibitions for debt collectors, including disclosures, validation notices, media restrictions, furnishing to credit reporting agencies, and dispute procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of accurate profile name when communicating online
rubrics_metrics.description: The debt collector must communicate using a profile that accurately identifies the debt collector's individual name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 1006.18(d). (Note: commentary references § 1006.18(f) re: assumed names.) Debt collector must also comply with requirements for obtaining location information in § 1006.10, communicating with third parties in § 1006.6(d)(1), and communicating through social media in § 1006.22(f)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited-content message is not a 'communication' for disclosure purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: A limited-content message, as defined in § 1006.2(j), is not a communication as defined in § 1006.2(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a voicemail contains only limited-content content, the collector need not make § 1006.18(e)(1) and (2) disclosures. But if voicemail adds other content that directly or indirectly conveys info regarding a debt, it becomes a communication and § 1006.18(e) disclosures are required. See commentary to § 1006.2(d) and (j).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial communication disclosure requirement (§1006.18(e)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector must make the disclosure required by § 1006.18(e)(1) in the debt collector's initial communication with a consumer, regardless of medium or who initiated contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: If consumer-initiated call is the first communication after a limited-content message, the collector must disclose during that call that it is attempting to collect a debt and that any information obtained will be used for that purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent communication disclosure requirement (§1006.18(e)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector must disclose in each subsequent communication that the communication is from a debt collector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A validation notice provided within five days of an initial telephone communication (per Model Form B-1) can satisfy the relevant disclosure requirements as described in comment 34(c)(1)-1 (collector may use either the §1006.18(e)(1) or (e)(2) disclosure in some situations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Translated disclosures must match communication language (§1006.18(e)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector must make the disclosures required by § 1006.18(e)(1) and (2) in the same language(s) used for the rest of the communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: If initial communication is in Spanish, the §1006.18(e)(1) disclosure must be in Spanish. If later communication is partly English and partly Spanish, the §1006.18(e)(2) disclosure must be provided in both languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted use of assumed names when readily identifiable (§1006.18(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: § 1006.18 does not prohibit an employee from using an assumed name if the debt collector can readily identify any employee using an assumed name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collector may manage assumed names by requiring consistent use of the same assumed name for an employee and preventing reuse by others, or by any other method that enables determination of true identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on language or symbols on envelopes (§1006.22(f)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector must not use any language or symbol, other than the debt collector's address, on any envelope when communicating by mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Language or symbol’ excludes items that facilitate mail delivery (debtor's name/address, postage, forwarding/address correction language, USPS Intelligent Mail barcode).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on emailing employer-provided addresses (§1006.22(f)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector must not communicate or attempt to communicate by sending an email to an address the collector knows was provided by the consumer's employer, with specified exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: permitted if email address falls under § 1006.6(d)(4)(i) or (iii) (consumer used that address to communicate about the debt, or provided prior consent); emails to addresses described in §1006.6(d)(4)(ii) remain prohibited. See §1006.6(d)(4) for detailed conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on public or contact-viewable social media communications (§1006.22(f)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector must not communicate or attempt to communicate about a debt through social media if the communication is viewable by the general public or the person's social media contacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Prohibits posting messages on a person's public social media page or to their social contacts. Sending a private message not viewable by public or contacts is not prohibited here, though other provisions (e.g., §1006.6(b), §1006.14(h)) may restrict or prohibit sending messages to the wrong person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not furnish to consumer reporting agency before taking required actions (§1006.30(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector must not furnish information about a debt to a consumer reporting agency before taking one of the actions described in § 1006.30(a)(1)(i) or (ii); validation information required by § 1006.34(c) counts as information about the debt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collector must ensure validation requirements satisfied before furnishing to CRAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable waiting period before furnishing after mailing/electronic message (§1006.30(a)(1)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector who mails a letter about a debt or sends an electronic message must wait a reasonable period to receive notice of undeliverability before furnishing information to a CRA; 14 consecutive days after mailing/sending is a reasonable period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reasonable period begins on the date the letter is mailed or electronic message sent. If no undeliverability notice received during that period, furnishing thereafter does not violate §1006.30(a)(1) even if a later undeliverability notice arrives.

rubrics_metrics.name: If notice of undeliverability received within waiting period, do not furnish until additional action taken
rubrics_metrics.description: If collector receives a notice of undeliverability during the reasonable period, the collector must not furnish information about the debt to a CRA until the collector otherwise satisfies §1006.30(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: If mailed validation notice on May 1 and undeliverability received May 10, furnishing thereafter without taking additional actions is a violation. If subsequent validation notice mailed and another reasonable period passes without undeliverability, furnishing is permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on transferring debts paid/settled/discharged in bankruptcy (§1006.30(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector may not transfer for consideration a debt that has been paid or settled or discharged in bankruptcy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfer for consideration means receiving or expecting compensation for the transfer. Sending data about the debt (analytics, scrubbing, archiving) is not a transfer for consideration. Reporting to a credit reporting agency that a debt was paid/settled/discharged is not a transfer for consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with FCRA prohibition on selling/transferring identity-theft debts
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in §1006.30(b)(1) alters a debt collector's obligation under FCRA §615(f)(1) that no person shall sell, transfer for consideration, or place for collection a debt notified as resulting from identity theft under section 605B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collectors must follow FCRA identity-theft protections in addition to Reg F.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited exception to transfer debts to the debt owner (§1006.30(b)(2)(i)(A))
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector collecting a debt described in §1006.30(b)(1) may transfer the debt to the debt's owner, but generally may not transfer it or the right to collect it to another entity on behalf of the owner unless another exception applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers to the owner are permitted; transfers to third parties for consideration are generally prohibited absent an exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation information must be provided by notice or orally in initial communication (§1006.34(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector generally must provide the validation information required by §1006.34(c) either by sending a validation notice in the manner required by §1006.42 or by providing the information orally in the debt collector's initial communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the collector knows or should know the consumer is deceased and has not previously provided validation info, a person authorized to act for the estate operates as the consumer and must receive the validation info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial communication excludes formal pleadings (bankruptcy proofs of claim) (§1006.34(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The term initial communication does not include a communication in the form of a formal pleading in a civil action; a proof of claim filed in bankruptcy pursuant to the Bankruptcy Code is not an initial communication for §1006.34.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bankruptcy filings are treated as formal pleadings, not initial communications for validation purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Itemization date: selectable reference dates and consistency (§1006.34(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Itemization date is any one of five reference dates (last statement date, charge-off date, last payment date, transaction date, judgment date). A debt collector may select any of these dates to comply, but once a collector uses a reference date for a debt in communications with a consumer, the collector must use that reference date consistently when providing §1006.34(c) information to that consumer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsequent debt collectors may use a different reference date than a prior collector. Examples and definitions of each reference date provided in comments (last statement date is last periodic statement or written invoice by creditor or third party; last payment date is when last payment applied; transaction date is date goods/services provided). If multiple transaction dates exist, collector may choose any but must use it consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation period duration and calculation (§1006.34(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Validation period starts on the date validation information is provided and ends 30 days after the consumer receives or is assumed to receive it; §1006.34(c)(3)(i)-(iii) require statements specifying the end date of the validation period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When validation information provided in writing/electronically, collector uses the assumed receipt date to calculate end date even if actual receipt differs. If subsequent validation notice sent because original was not received, collector must calculate validation period based on receipt/assumed receipt of subsequent notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation information must include debt-collector disclosure (§1006.34(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Validation information includes the statement required by §1006.18(e): the initial-communication disclosure (§1006.18(e)(1)) and the subsequent-communication disclosure (§1006.18(e)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A validation notice provided as described in §1006.34(a)(1)(i)(A) complies with §1006.34(c)(1) by providing the §1006.18(e)(1) disclosure; a notice under §1006.34(a)(1)(i)(B) may provide either §1006.18(e)(1) or §1006.18(e)(2). Model Form B-1 examples discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation info must include debt collector name and acceptable variants (§1006.34(c)(2)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Validation information includes the debt collector's name; the collector may disclose its trade or doing-business-as name instead of its legal name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mailing address must be the address at which collector accepts disputes and requests for original-creditor information; vendor addresses are acceptable if they meet that function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide consumer's most complete and accurate name (§1006.34(c)(2)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Validation information must include the version of the consumer's name the collector reasonably determines is the most complete and accurate based on the collector's knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omitting known name information that creates a false, misleading, or confusing impression about identity fails the requirement. Example: If creditor provided first, middle, last, and suffix, collector must include all; omission would not satisfy §1006.34(c)(2)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Creditor name disclosure rules (§1006.34(c)(2)(iii) & (v))
rubrics_metrics.description: If collecting debt related to a consumer financial product/service, validation information includes the name of the creditor to whom the debt was owed on the itemization date and the name of the creditor to whom the debt currently is owed; trade/DBA names may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two separate creditor-name disclosures: per itemization date and current creditor. Use of trade names permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account number disclosure and truncation recognizability (§1006.34(c)(2)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: Validation information includes the account number associated with the debt on the itemization date, or a truncated version; truncated account number must remain recognizable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: truncating a credit-card number to last four digits is permissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amount on itemization date includes fees, interest, and charges (§1006.34(c)(2)(vii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Validation information includes the amount of the debt on the itemization date, including any fees, interest, or other charges owed as of that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collector must calculate amount as of selected itemization date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Itemization of current amount must reflect interest, fees, payments, credits (§1006.34(c)(2)(viii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Validation information must include an itemization of the current amount reflecting interest, fees, payments, and credits since the itemization date; fields for all these items must appear even if none have been assessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collector may indicate '0', 'none', or state no interest/fees/payments/credits have been applied; required fields may not be left blank. If another law requires an itemization substantially similar to Model Form B-1, that itemization may be used instead. Itemization may be on a separate page if the notice includes a reference statement where the itemization would have appeared. Combining multiple debts on a single validation notice may use a single cumulative itemization or separate itemizations on separate pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current amount definition and multiple-debt treatment (§1006.34(c)(2)(ix))
rubrics_metrics.description: Validation information includes the current amount of the debt (amount as of when validation info provided). For combined multiple debts on a single validation notice, collector may disclose a single cumulative figure that sums the current amounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For residential mortgage debt subject to Reg Z, collector may comply by providing total balance including principal, interest, fees, and other charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic validation notices must state how to dispute/request original-creditor info electronically (§1006.34(c)(3)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: If providing the validation notice electronically, validation information includes a statement explaining how a consumer can electronically dispute the debt or request original-creditor information, naming an email address or website portal that consumer can use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collector may provide information about only one medium even if it accepts multiple, but may provide multiple if desired. Suggested phrasing: 'We accept disputes electronically at' followed by address/portal and similar for original creditor requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer-response prompts formatting (§1006.34(c)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: If validation information is provided in writing or electronically, a prompt required by §1006.34(c)(4) may be formatted as a checkbox as in Model Form B-1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model Form B-1 demonstrates acceptable prompt formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special rule for residential mortgage debt (use of recent periodic statement) (§1006.34(c)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: For residential mortgage debt subject to Regulation Z, a collector need not provide certain itemization fields (c)(2)(vi)-(viii) if the collector provides the most recent periodic statement required under Reg Z in the same communication and includes a statement on the validation notice referring to that periodic statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example referral language: 'See the enclosed periodic statement for an itemization of the debt.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe harbor for Model Form B-1 and 'substantially similar' forms (§1006.34(d)(2) & (d)(2)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A collector who provides a validation notice that is a Model Form B-1 or a substantially similar notice in substance, clarity, and meaningful sequence retains a safe harbor for compliance with §1006.34(c) and (d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible changes that retain safe harbor include removing language that could suggest liability if inapplicable, relocating consumer-response info to facilitate mailing, adding barcodes/QR codes (if not violating §1006.38(b)), adding the date the form is generated, and embedding hyperlinks if delivered electronically. A form neither matching Model Form B-1 nor substantially similar does not receive the safe harbor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional disclosures allowed on validation notices (§1006.34(d)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Collectors may include optional telephone contact information (number and times accepted) and disclosures required or providing safe harbors under applicable law on the reverse of the validation notice or below the notice if delivered by email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If including such disclosures on reverse/below, the front of the notice must include a referring statement (e.g., 'Notice: See reverse side for important information' or 'Notice: See below for important information'). Time-barred debt disclosures that applicable law requires may be included on the front if the applicable law specifies content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spanish-language supplemental information permitted (§1006.34(d)(3)(vi))
rubrics_metrics.description: Collector may include supplemental information in Spanish specifying how a consumer may request a Spanish-language validation notice (e.g., include Spanish statement that a consumer can request a Spanish-language validation notice by telephone or email).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when collector accepts requests through those communication media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted inclusion of merchant/affinity/facility brand on notice (§1006.34(d)(3)(vii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Collector may include the merchant brand, affinity brand, or facility name associated with the debt on the validation notice (e.g., 'XYZ Store', 'College of Columbia', 'ABC Hospital').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are optional supplemental identifiers to help consumers identify the debt's origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe harbor for complete and accurate translations (§1006.34(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a collector sends a validation notice translated into another language, the translation must be complete and accurate; translations provided on the Bureau's website are considered complete and accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collectors may use other translations if they are complete and accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'in writing' for disputes and original-creditor requests (§1006.38)
rubrics_metrics.description: A consumer has disputed the debt or requested the original creditor's name/address in writing if the consumer mails the dispute/request; returns the consumer-response form on the validation notice indicating the dispute/request; provides the dispute/request via an electronic medium through which collector accepts electronic communications (email or website portal); or delivers the dispute/request in person or by courier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This implements §1006.38's requirements for timely written disputes/requests and aligns with E-SIGN Act interpretations in comment 38-1.iii.

rubrics_metrics.name: E-SIGN Act interpretation enabling electronic 'writing' for §809(b) purposes (comment 38-1.iii)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bureau interprets section 101 of the E-SIGN Act as enabling a consumer to satisfy through an electronic request the FDCPA's section 809(b) requirement that the consumer's notification be 'in writing', provided the consumer uses an electronic medium the debt collector accepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because consumer may only use a medium the collector accepts, section 101(b) of E-SIGN is not contravened; thus electronic submissions are valid when collector accepts them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deceased-consumer rule for disputes/requests (§1006.38 and §1006.34(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: If collector knows or should know the consumer is deceased and the consumer has not previously disputed the debt or requested original-creditor information, a person authorized to act for the deceased consumer's estate operates as the consumer for purposes of §1006.38 and §1006.34(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collector must provide validation information to an individual identified by name who is authorized to act on behalf of the deceased consumer's estate.
